title: Aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (SAH)
subject: neurology
summary: Thunderclap headache needs CT, with LP if CT beyond 6 hours is negative; secure the aneurysm within 24 hours, avoid severe hypertension, hypotension and BP swings before securing, give oral nimodipine 60 mg every 4 hours for 21 days, keep euvolaemia and watch for delayed cerebral ischaemia on days 4 to 14.

sections.title: Recognise
items: Sudden severe headache reaching maximum within seconds to 1 hour, with or without vomiting, neck stiffness, collapse, seizure or focal deficit. A warning (sentinel) headache precedes 10 to 43% of cases.

Ottawa SAH rule (alert, age over 15, new severe non-traumatic headache peaking within 1 hour): investigate if age 40 or more, neck pain or stiffness, witnessed loss of consciousness, onset during exertion, instantly peaking pain, or limited neck flexion.
Grade at presentation with GCS and WFNS or Hunt and Hess; the grade guides prognosis and shared decisions.
ECG changes, raised troponin (stress cardiomyopathy) and neurogenic pulmonary oedema can mislead toward a primary cardiac diagnosis.

sections.title: Diagnosis
items: Non-contrast CT immediately. Within 6 hours of onset in a patient without a new deficit, a normal CT on a high-quality scanner read by an experienced neuroradiologist reasonably excludes SAH.
Presenting beyond 6 hours, or with a new neurological deficit, and CT negative: lumbar puncture (often performed 6 to 12 hours or more after onset) for xanthochromia and red cell count.
CT angiography to find the aneurysm; digital subtraction angiography if CTA is negative or inconclusive with high suspicion, and to plan treatment.
Bloods: CBC, coagulation, sodium and other electrolytes, glucose, renal function, troponin, group and crossmatch; 12-lead ECG.

sections.title: Before the aneurysm is secured
items: Transfer early to a high-volume centre with neurosurgery, neurointervention and neurocritical care.
Airway: intubate if GCS 8 or less. Head up 30 degrees, analgesia (paracetamol, cautious opioid), antiemetic, bed rest, stool softener.

BP: frequent monitoring and short-acting titratable drugs to avoid severe hypertension, hypotension and variability. No target is proven; many units keep systolic below 160 mmHg. Lower gradually if systolic is above 180 to 200 mmHg and keep MAP at least 65 mmHg.
Reverse any anticoagulant immediately (see the ICH protocol). Routine tranexamic acid is not recommended (no functional benefit in ULTRA).
Acute symptomatic hydrocephalus (falling consciousness, enlarged ventricles): urgent CSF diversion with EVD or lumbar drain.
Start enteral nimodipine as soon as possible after diagnosis.

sections.title: Definitive treatment and prevention of complications
items: Secure the ruptured aneurysm by coiling or clipping (neurovascular team decision) as early as feasible, preferably within 24 hours of onset, aiming for complete obliteration.
Nimodipine 60 mg orally or by nasogastric tube every 4 hours for 21 days. If it causes hypotension, give 30 mg every 2 hours (same daily dose) rather than stopping.
Maintain euvolaemia with isotonic fluids and goal-directed volume assessment. Prophylactic hypervolaemia or haemodynamic augmentation is harmful.

New seizures: antiseizure medication for 7 days. No routine prophylaxis (consider only with high-risk features such as MCA aneurysm, ICH, high grade, hydrocephalus or cortical infarction). Avoid phenytoin.
VTE: mechanical prophylaxis from admission; pharmacological prophylaxis (UFH or LMWH) once the aneurysm is secured.
Do not use routine statins or IV magnesium. Control glucose (avoid hyperglycaemia and hypoglycaemia) and treat fever.

sections.title: Monitoring for delayed cerebral ischaemia (DCI)
items: DCI affects about 30%, mostly on days 4 to 14: a new focal deficit or a fall of 2 or more GCS points lasting at least 1 hour, not explained by another cause.
Hourly neurological checks by trained nurses. Transcranial Doppler monitoring is reasonable; CTA or CT perfusion if DCI is suspected or the examination is limited; continuous EEG in high-grade SAH.
Before labelling DCI, exclude rebleeding, hydrocephalus, hyponatraemia, hypoxia, fever, infection and seizures.
Check sodium at least daily: hyponatraemia (cerebral salt wasting or SIADH) is common. Do not fluid restrict; mineralocorticoids (fludrocortisone) are reasonable for natriuresis and hyponatraemia.

sections.title: Treating DCI and rebleeding
items: Symptomatic vasospasm or DCI: raise systolic BP (vasopressor such as noradrenaline) while keeping euvolaemia, and reassess the neurological response.
Severe refractory vasospasm: intra-arterial vasodilator therapy or angioplasty in a neurointerventional centre.
Sudden deterioration or new severe headache before securing: suspect rebleeding; urgent CT and neurosurgical review.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Discharging a thunderclap headache after a normal CT done beyond 6 hours without LP or angiography.
Stopping nimodipine for hypotension instead of splitting the dose; excessive BP lowering causing ischaemia.
Fluid restriction for hyponatraemia, which raises the risk of DCI.
Missing SAH that presents with seizure, syncope or neck pain alone, or treating the ECG and troponin as a primary myocardial infarction.
Using phenytoin for seizure prophylaxis.

drugs.name: Nimodipine
drugs.dose: 60 mg orally or by NG tube every 4 hours for 21 days
drugs.notes: If hypotension: 30 mg every 2 hours. Enteral route is the recommended route.

drugs.name: Labetalol
drugs.dose: 10 to 20 mg IV over 1 to 2 minutes, may repeat; or infusion 2 to 8 mg/min
drugs.notes: Short-acting control of severe hypertension before securing; avoid hypotension.

drugs.name: Nicardipine
drugs.dose: 5 mg/h IV infusion, increase by 2.5 mg/h every 5 to 15 minutes, max 15 mg/h

drugs.name: Paracetamol
drugs.dose: 1 g orally or IV every 6 hours (max 4 g/day)
drugs.notes: Analgesia and fever; reduce max dose in low weight or liver disease.

drugs.name: Levetiracetam
drugs.dose: 500 to 1000 mg orally or IV twice daily for 7 days
drugs.notes: For new seizures after SAH; reduce in renal impairment. Avoid phenytoin.
